concepts.def: Sacrament of bread and wine commemorating Last Supper; Catholic transubstantiation, Protestant memorial or real presence.
Sacrament of initiation; Catholics infant baptism, Baptists believers' baptism by full immersion; Matthew 28 commands it.
Religious journey to sacred sites; Christians visit Jerusalem (Holy Sepulchre), Lourdes (Marian apparitions), Walsingham.
Liturgical (Catholic Mass, Anglican Eucharist) or non-liturgical (Quaker silence, evangelical praise); 'in spirit and truth' (John 4:24).
Feast of the Nativity on 25 December (most churches); celebrates Incarnation; Advent season of preparation precedes.
Most important Christian festival; celebrates Resurrection; preceded by Holy Week, Good Friday, Lent fasting (40 days).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Christianity: Practices — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Christianity: Practices brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Christianity: Practices.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

numericals.q: On what date is Christmas celebrated?
